tweet_summary: Syria analyst Charles Lister quotes a screenshot from X user @EgidSerzan threatening to 'erase' Arab tribes in Qamishli, attributing the statement to an 'SDF commander' during the Hasakah/Qamishli fighting.
why_note_decision: Multiple credible voices in the reply thread, including Kurdish journalist/analyst Frederike Geerdink, Kurdish analyst Kamal Chomani (cited in the original note), and others, say @EgidSerzan is not an SDF/YPG commander — just a private X user. No reputable English-language source identifies him as a commander, and there is no corroboration in the major outlets covering the Hasakah/Qamishli clashes. On a 263K-impression post by a 219K-follower Syria analyst, an attribution-correction note is warranted.
judge_guidance: PASS if the note (1) states the 'SDF commander' attribution for the @EgidSerzan post is unverified / disputed, AND (2) cites at least one credible Kurdish journalist/analyst or outlet noting he is not a known SDF commander (e.g., Kamal Chomani's post, Frederike Geerdink reply, Al Jazeera reporting that does not corroborate). FAIL if the note: asserts the threat itself is fabricated (the post exists), defends Lister's attribution, or denies the Syria-government / SDF context entirely.
reference_note: Attributing an 'erase you' threat to an SDF commander is unverified. Kurdish analysts including Kamal Chomani say the post comes from a private/non-SDF account, and major outlets covering the Hasakah/Qamishli fighting do not corroborate the quote as coming from any SDF commander. https://x.com/KamalChomani/status/2013507206046417292 https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/3/syrian-forces-enter-qamishli-under-ceasefire-deal-with-sdf-state-media

fact_check.notes: EgidSerzan does not appear in any reputable English source as an SDF commander. Multiple Kurdish observers in the thread reject the attribution; Lister has not provided corroborating evidence.

importance.lens_rationale: War-zone misattribution from a prominent Syria analyst risks inflaming inter-ethnic violence. Correcting it is valuable for accurate conflict reporting standards.
